item.title: WAEC: 56,000 candidates register for 2026 private WASSCE
item.description: The West African Examinations Council (WAEC) says no fewer than 56,000 candidates registered for the 2026 West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) for Private Candidates (Second Series). The Head, National Office (HNO), WAEC, Mr Suleiman Kum, disclosed this during an inspection of the Computer-Based Test (CBT) English Language examination on Saturday in Lagos. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the inspection took place at the WAEC Training and Testing Centre, Ijaiye Road, Ogba, where candidates sat for the examination. Kum said that the registered candidates included about 272 walk-in candidates who enrolled to remedy individual subjects. He said that Lagos State recorded more than 22,000 candidates, including about 50 walk-in candidates sitting for the examination. The WAEC official said that the adoption of CBT was enabling the curbing of examination malpractices, strengthening the credibility of the exercise and promoting transparency. He said that WAEC introduced CBT in 2024 and had continued to improve the process to strengthen examination security and reduce malpractice. “We have discovered that computer-based tests, popularly known as CBT, are truly the best way to conduct examinations because malpractice is drastically reduced,” Kum said. He said that candidates were thoroughly searched before entering examination halls to prevent prohibited materials from being taken inside and safeguard the integrity of the exercise. “We do not set traps for candidates; we want to prevent malpractice by ensuring they enter the examination hall without unauthorised materials,” Kum said. He said that the council would continue to adopt innovations to improve examination administration and sustain its reputation for integrity. “WAEC will continue to improve to ensure that it remains the benchmark for examination integrity and innovation in Nigeria,” Kum said. The HNO advised candidates to study diligently, practise WAEC past questions and marking schemes, and read chief examiners’ reports to improve their performance. “The chief examiners’ reports show candidates’ weaknesses, strengths and how they should answer questions, which can greatly improve their performance,” he said. NAN also reports that the examination is part of WAEC’s ongoing transition toward computer-based testing. The party said the discrepancy demands urgent answers, especially as Nigerians battling rising living costs are forced to account for every naira while the government faces questions over the country’s foreign earnings. According to the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, the country recorded a $12 billion current-account surplus and $6.2 billion in net financial inflows in the first half of the year. The report, however, identified a $12.4 billion gap in Nigeria’s external accounts. item.title: In-form Atletico snatch late win at Espanyol
item.description: Alex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch Atletico Madrid a 1-0 win at Espanyol and put pressure on La Liga leaders Barcelona on Saturday. Diego Simeone’s side, second, moved two points behind Hansi Flick’s champions, who visit third-placed Real Betis later on. Spain international Baena smashed home from the edge of the box to claim the Rojiblancos an important late victory from a tight game in Cornella. Atletico have won six consecutive games across all competitions. “They had a good game defensively and it was hard for us,” Baena told DAZN. “The good thing this team has is that it keeps believing until the 90th minute.” Baena, who struggled last season but has been in fine fettle since winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, hugged coach Simeone after finding the net. “He’s a player who can do a lot of damage, who is in very good form,” Simeone told DAZN after Baena’s fifth league goal of the season. Both sides had chances in the first half but Espanyol came closest as Leandro Cabrera struck the crossbar. Marcos Llorente hit the same woodwork after an hour with a long-range effort for Atletico. Espanyol brought on captain Javi Puado after a long-term knee injury, as he made his first appearance since January. Julian Alvarez was bright for Atletico as a substitute as he continues to find his form after trying to force a move away in the summer. Atletico have left it late several times this season to claim points and did so again here, with Baena thumping home from Alvarez’s pass to earn his team’s victory. “Last year (Baena) started well but then injuries prevented him from reaching his best form and having the season he wanted,” Simeone told reporters. “The World Cup took him to a different place, he sees football differently than others and (now) he’s more confident and stronger, he’s the player we went looking for.” Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak made a good save in stoppage time from Pol Lozano to ensure his team kept the three points. On Sunday Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla among other fixtures. AFP The post In-form Atletico snatch late win at Espanyol appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Some Lagos-based lawyers on Saturday, warned hospitals and healthcare providers against demanding upfront payments before treating patients in medical emergencies. The lawyers told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that such actions violate the National Health Act of 2014, and attract legal sanctions. They argue that section 20(1) of the Act prohibited healthcare providers, health workers and health establishments from refusing emergency medical treatment for any reason, including a patient’s inability to pay a deposit. The lawyers, however, called for effective healthcare financing and reimbursement mechanisms, to protect hospitals from financial losses while ensuring that patients received timely medical attention. An Associate of the Institute of Medical and Health Law, Ms Odinichionye Egwuenu, told NAN that the law was clear that emergency treatment must not be withheld because a patient could not make upfront payment. She urged hospitals to notify the nearest police station within two hours of commencing treatment in compliance with the law, The lawyer also called for institutional safeguards to protect medical practitioners who disregarded internal payment policies to fulfil their professional obligations to emergency patients. She, consequently, called for the strengthening of emergency healthcare funding, establishing effective reimbursement mechanisms as well as providing lawful avenues for recovering outstanding medical expenses. On his part, another lawyer, Mr Spurgeon Ataene, said doctors had an ethical obligation to prioritise saving lives in emergency situations before turning their attention to payment. Ataene said demanding payment before attending to a patient in a life-threatening condition, could amount to professional misconduct and potentially expose the practitioner to disciplinary action. He added that denying emergency care on financial grounds could also raise concerns about the patient’s fundamental right to life. Ataene specifically stressed that gunshot victims should be treated before questions were asked about the circumstances of their injuries. “It will therefore, be unethical for a doctor to make a demand for payment before treatment; He could be sanctioned and may lose his license,” he said Ataene, however, acknowledged that patients should pay for medical services, particularly in non-emergency situations, noting that hospitals required funds to maintain equipment, pay staff and provide a clean and orderly environment. He urged lawmakers to strengthen legislation requiring healthcare providers to stabilise emergency patients before making payment demands or conducting further inquiries that could delay treatment. Similarly, another Lagos-based lawyer, Mrs Jumoke Ajayi of Olorunwapelumi Chambers, warned that healthcare providers could face criminal sanctions for refusing emergency medical treatment over unpaid bills. Ajayi cited Section 20(2) of the National Health Act, which prescribes a fine of N100,000, imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months, or both, for contravening the provision on emergency medical treatment. She explained that patients suffering from serious injuries sustained in road accidents, severe bleeding or other life-threatening conditions were entitled to immediate medical attention, irrespective of their financial circumstances. “The legal position is that the hospital must attend to the patient’s emergency medical needs without refusing treatment on financial grounds,” she said. Ajayi, however, clarified that the law did not automatically exempt patients from paying their medical bills, adding that hospitals could subsequently seek payment for services provided, subject to applicable laws and relevant payment arrangements. According to her, determining whether a hospital or healthcare worker had committed an offence would depend on the circumstances and available evidence, including whether treatment was refused, delayed or referred to another facility. Meanwhile, Ajayi noted that healthcare workers could not be held liable for consequences arising from their inability to provide particular emergency services where a hospital lacked the necessary equipment or capacity to handle the case. Besides, she noted that the law protected patients’ access to emergency care but did not require every form of medical treatment to be provided free of charge. On the whole, the lawyers maintained that protecting patients’ lives and sustaining healthcare institutions should not be competing objectives. They consequently, urging government and relevant stakeholders to develop a system that guarantees emergency treatment while providing hospitals with adequate financial support. item.title: Egypt’s president says country ready to defend Saudi Arabia ‘if requested’
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on Saturday said Egypt was ready to defend Saudi Arabia “if requested”, as fighting flares between the kingdom and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. Since Yemen’s war reignited in July, the Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week. The Houthis have also blockaded the Bab al-Mandab Strait, piling pressure on energy exports as Iran presses its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian military academy, Sisi said Egypt was “not looking for a role to play” in regional conflicts, but added that it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was “harmed or its security and stability threatened”. “Egypt, of course, with the directives of His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will carry out any measure to protect you or defend you,” he said. He added that any deployment would require parliamentary approval and said he hoped lawmakers would convene in an emergency session to grant authorisation “if it is requested of us”. “I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone,” Sisi said. “We are speaking only about defence.” During a visit to Egypt last month, de facto Saudi leader Mohammed bin Salman and Sisi called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea, a vital trade route. The conflict with the Houthis poses risks not only to Saudi Arabia’s security and energy exports, but also to Egypt, where disruption to Red Sea shipping could further reduce revenues from the Suez Canal, a key source of foreign currency. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said last month that Egypt’s Suez Canal lost about $11 billion in revenues since the Houthis began attacking commercial vessels following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. Despite its longstanding military ties with Gulf states, Egypt has not joined the Mecca agreement, a mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in August, with Cairo generally favouring diplomacy over participation in regional military alliances. Saudi Arabia has long been a key backer of Egypt, providing financial support after the 2013 ouster of Islamist late president Mohammed Morsi and during subsequent economic crises. item.title: Neto double gives Chelsea win; marred by Martinez injury
item.description: Pedro Neto’s double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emi Martinez to a head injury. Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the three points during the 11 added minutes following the lengthy treatment given to the stricken Martinez. The Argentine international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital. Victory lifts Chelsea above the Toffees into the top four of the Premier League. After a slow start, a fiery-tempered encounter sparked into life when Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong launched into a tackle on Josh Acheampong for the first of five first-half yellow cards. That challenge also enlivened the home crowd and spurred Everton on to their best spell of the game. Thierno Barry was guilty of another wasteful day in front of goal as the Frenchman planted a header from Jack Grealish’s cross too close to Martinez. Chelsea have made a habit of fast starts under Xabi Alonso, but it took until four minutes before half-time to threaten when Moises Caicedo blasted off the bar from a well-worked corner. Everton were furious that Morgan Rogers escaped a second booking just before the break after a thunderous clash with England team-mate James Garner. That proved to be a huge decision as the visitors this time flew out of the blocks at the start of the second period. Jorrel Hato got to the byline and his low cross fell to Neto, who had time to control before firing low past Pickford. Chelsea had not kept a Premier League clean sheet in 22 matches stretching back to January, but were rarely troubled by an Everton side short on forward options despite the loss of Martinez. The treatment for the goalkeeper threatened to halt Chelsea’s momentum as they controlled the second half. Belgian Mike Penders replaced Martinez for his first Premier League appearance but had little to do bar dealing with a few desperate Everton crosses. At the other end Pickford made a fine save to deny Joao Pedro. But Chelsea did get their second goal when Neto coolly stroked into the bottom corner after Jordan Henderson’s free-kick was blocked by the Everton wall. item.title: FG destroys over 19,000 illicit weapons in anti-terrorism drive — Ribadu
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki The Federal Government has disclosed that it has destroyed more than 19,000 illicit weapons since 2022 as part of sustained efforts to dismantle the operational capacity of terrorists, bandits and other criminal networks threatening Nigeria’s security. The National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, disclosed this on Saturday in Sokoto during a high-level brainstorming session on tackling banditry in Sokoto State, stressing that the government was intensifying efforts to stem the proliferation of illegal firearms and restore lasting peace to vulnerable communities. The dialogue, themed “Coping with Banditry in Sokoto State: A Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue for Prevention, Containment and Community Resilience,” was convened by the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) in collaboration with the Centre for Peace Studies, Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto. It brought security concerns, community resilience and coordinated action to the forefront of discussions on addressing insecurity in the North-West. Ribadu, who was represented by Barrister Zakariyya Mijinyawa, said the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was strengthening the national security architecture through intensified military operations, intelligence gathering, law enforcement, border surveillance and improved inter-agency collaboration. He maintained that defeating banditry required a coordinated strategy capable of dismantling criminal networks, disrupting their supply chains and preventing armed groups from exploiting security gaps. He identified Operation FANSAN YAMMA as a critical platform for coordinating security operations across the North-West, noting that sustained pressure on criminal elements remained necessary to protect lives, secure communities and prevent armed groups from establishing safe havens. item.content:encoded: By Musa Ubandawaki The Federal Government has disclosed that it has destroyed more than 19,000 illicit weapons since 2022 as part of sustained efforts to dismantle the operational capacity of terrorists, bandits and other criminal networks threatening Nigeria’s security. The National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, disclosed this on Saturday in Sokoto during a high-level brainstorming session on tackling banditry in Sokoto State, stressing that the government was intensifying efforts to stem the proliferation of illegal firearms and restore lasting peace to vulnerable communities. The dialogue, themed “Coping with Banditry in Sokoto State: A Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue for Prevention, Containment and Community Resilience,” was convened by the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) in collaboration with the Centre for Peace Studies, Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto. It brought security concerns, community resilience and coordinated action to the forefront of discussions on addressing insecurity in the North-West. Ribadu, who was represented by Barrister Zakariyya Mijinyawa, said the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was strengthening the national security architecture through intensified military operations, intelligence gathering, law enforcement, border surveillance and improved inter-agency collaboration. He maintained that defeating banditry required a coordinated strategy capable of dismantling criminal networks, disrupting their supply chains and preventing armed groups from exploiting security gaps. He identified Operation FANSAN YAMMA as a critical platform for coordinating security operations across the North-West, noting that sustained pressure on criminal elements remained necessary to protect lives, secure communities and prevent armed groups from establishing safe havens. He said the government would continue to reinforce operational cooperation among security agencies to confront emerging threats across the region. Highlighting recent weapons-control operations, the NSA cited figures from the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons (NCCSALW), whose Director-General, retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police Johnson Kokumo, was identified in his remarks. According to Ribadu, the centre recovered 5,449 firearms and destroyed 1,419 illicit weapons during nationwide operations in September 2026, underscoring the continuing challenge posed by illegal arms trafficking. “These figures demonstrate the importance of sustained weapons-control operations. The NCCSALW and relevant security agencies will continue to strengthen efforts to disrupt arms-trafficking networks, trace recovered weapons and prevent illicit firearms from reaching criminal groups,” he said. Ribadu, however, cautioned that military action and weapons seizures alone would not deliver sustainable peace unless accompanied by effective governance and a sustained government presence in communities recovered from criminal groups. He argued that security operations must be backed by measures that restore public confidence, rebuild local institutions and enable displaced and vulnerable populations to resume their normal lives without the constant threat of violence. To strengthen coordination, he said the Office of the National Security Adviser was advancing a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach through the National Crisis Management Doctrine (NCMD). The framework, he explained, was designed to improve preparedness, strengthen collaboration among relevant institutions and ensure that security responses were coordinated rather than fragmented across government agencies and community structures. Addressing the peculiar security challenges confronting Sokoto State, Ribadu called for intelligence-led operations to deny bandits access to safe havens around vulnerable settlements, forest corridors and border communities. He stressed the importance of supporting State Forest Guards and NSCDC Agro-Rangers as part of broader efforts to improve surveillance, protect rural populations and disrupt the movement of criminal groups. He also underscored the need for stronger cross-border intelligence-sharing and functional early-warning mechanisms linking local authorities, traditional rulers, community leaders and security focal points. According to him, timely reporting and rapid responses to credible security alerts would be crucial to preventing attacks and protecting residents in vulnerable areas, including Sabon Birni, Isa, Tangaza and Goronyo. The NSA further called for stronger community participation in the fight against banditry, warning that misinformation, economic hardship and the vulnerability of young people could undermine security interventions if left unaddressed. He urged stakeholders to protect livelihoods, expand access to education and employment opportunities, and develop community-based measures capable of discouraging youth recruitment into criminal networks. “Reintegration must never replace justice or reward violence. His position highlighted the need to balance opportunities for peace with justice for victims and measures to prevent the recurrence of violence. He commended the Sokoto Advancement Forum (SAF) for developing its Blueprint for the Strategic Development of Sokoto State, urging participants to translate the dialogue into measurable actions rather than allowing the discussions to end as another policy exercise without practical consequences. He specifically called for the development of a community security and early-warning plan that would establish clear responsibilities, improve information-sharing and strengthen cooperation between residents and security agencies. “Let this dialogue mark a decisive step towards a safer Sokoto where communities live without fear, agriculture and commerce flourish, young people pursue productive lives, and public institutions protect every citizen,” Ribadu said. He maintained that restoring security in Sokoto and the wider North-West would require sustained commitment, collective responsibility and a comprehensive strategy that combines military pressure, intelligence-driven policing, effective governance, economic opportunity and community resilience. item.title: Ex-Senegal president Macky Sall withdraws as candidate for UN leader
item.description: Former president of Senegal Macky Sall on Saturday withdrew from the seven-person race to be the next UN secretary-general, a day after an informal UN Security Council poll produced no clear favourite. In a statement released on social media, Sall said he had noted the result of the poll and “hoped to contribute now the emergence of a consensus candidate within the Security Council”. He added that “the results of different test votes indicate a choice favouring a candidate — perhaps female –from the Latin America-Caribbean region.” A UN diplomat said Friday that all seven hopefuls had received a vote of “discourage,” effectively a veto, from a permanent UN Security Council member in anonymous informal polling. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan — who has been among the frontrunners in five previous polls — received the most “encourage” votes, but also got five “discourage” votes, including two from permanent members of the 15-country council. US media reports suggest Washington opposes all seven contenders. Among those considered by diplomats to be potential entrants are Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under the US-backed “Board of Peace,” and the UAE’s minister of state for foreign affairs Lana Nusseibeh. Turkey’s Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, secretary general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), has also had his name floated. The other candidates are Guyanese ex-foreign minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, Argentina’s Rafael Grossi, who heads the UN nuclear watchdog, Ecuador’s Ivonne A-Baki and Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu. The outgoing secretary-general, Antonio Guterres of Portugal, ends his second five-year term on December 31. Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided. item.title: Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion — Makinde
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country. item.title: Police rescue baby allegedly sold by mother for N2m
item.description: The Police Command in Oyo State has rescued a one-month-old baby girl, allegedly sold by her mother for N2 million to one Folawewo in Ido Local Government Area of Ibadan. The Police Publicity Relations Officer (PPRO), DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, made this known in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday in Ibadan. Ayanlade alleged that the health facility owner facilitated the sale of the baby girl after her mother delivered there. The PPRO said that a woman, Mary Amos, reported the incident to the police on Thursday, at about 6.00 p.m. The complainant, said the police spokesperson, claimed that her 23-year-old daughter gave birth to a baby girl on Sept. 6 at Ebepraise Health Centre, Ido. “She further reported that her daughter disappeared with the baby about seven days after delivery and could not provide a satisfactory account of the child’s whereabouts, raising suspicions that the baby might have been sold. “Acting on the report, police operatives arrested the baby’s mother for questioning. “She confessed during interrogation that the owner of the health facility and one Oludunni lured her into the arrangement and facilitated the sale of the baby to one Folawewo,” he said. Ayanlade said investigations later revealed that the baby’s mother received N1 million of the N2 million, while the health facility owner and Oludunni received N500,000 each. According to him, the one-month-old baby girl has been rescued, and efforts are currently ongoing to arrest the buyer of the baby, Folawemo, and all other persons involved to face justice. He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons. He also urged members of the public to promptly report any suspected cases of child trafficking and related offences. item.title: Top 5 African countries with the most visa-free travel if you own their passport
item.description: African passports differ significantly in the number of destinations their holders can visit without obtaining a visa before departure, with Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa leading the continent in international travel access. The Henley Passport Index, which uses data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA), ranks passports according to the number of destinations their holders can access without a prior visa. Its 2026 rankings place Seychelles among Africa’s strongest passports, followed by Mauritius and South Africa. Based on the 2026 rankings and available passport-mobility data, here are five African countries whose passports offer extensive international travel access. Seychelles Seychelles has one of Africa’s most powerful passports, giving its citizens broad access to destinations across the world without securing a visa in advance. The island nation retained its position as Africa’s leading passport in the 2026 Henley Passport Index, ranking among the top 25 passports globally in the July update. According to the Seychelles News Agency, the passport provided visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 155 destinations at that time. Its international mobility gives Seychellois citizens greater flexibility when planning holidays, business trips and other short-term journeys abroad. The country’s position reflects the benefits of its international relations and the travel arrangements it has established with other countries. item.title: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A former spokesperson to ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande has dismissed claims by Babachir Lawal that former President Muhammadu Buhari considered Osinbajo’s 2023 presidential ambition “highly immoral and distasteful”. Akande, who served as Osinbajo’s spokesperson from 2015 to 2023, described the allegation as false in a statement on Saturday, saying Buhari had personally offered to support the former vice-president’s ambition on at least four occasions. Osinbajo contested the All Progressives Congress presidential primary in 2022 but lost to Bola Tinubu, who went on to win the 2023 presidential election. Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, ADC, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, had alleged in a recent interview that Buhari would have found it difficult to support Osinbajo’s ambition because of his longstanding relationship with Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor. Reacting, Akande said he had watched the interview in which Lawal made allegations against Osinbajo and chose to respond because he was present when decisions concerning the former vice-president’s office were taken. He said Buhari had, on at least four separate occasions, personally offered to support Osinbajo, asking him, “If I don’t support you, who will I support?” “He was consistent. During the APC presidential primaries in 2022, while campaigns were underway, President Buhari openly commended Vice President Osinbajo at a Federal Executive Council meeting for the dignified, issues-based manner in which he was conducting his campaign across the country. He spoke in a laudatory tone. The entire Council witnessed it.” “That is not a President who found Osinbajo’s ambition distasteful. That is a President who broached it, encouraged and applauded it,” Akande added. Osinbajo contested the APC presidential primary in June 2022, finishing third with 235 votes, behind now president Bola Tinubu, who won with 1,271 votes, and Rotimi Amaechi, who scored 316.
